layers.title: Probability of a Pseudo-nitzschia bloom
layers.threshold_text: Probability that Pseudo-nitzschia exceeds 10,000 cells per litre
layers.description: Chance that cells of Pseudo-nitzschia, the diatom that can produce domoic acid, exceed 10,000 per litre in surface water.

time.issued_date_method: nowcast valid day + 1 day (one run issues all leads)

freshness.note: C-HARM runs daily but runs are often missing. Current: issued today or yesterday (UTC). Stale: 2-7 days old. Historical: older than 7 days; not a current forecast.

caveats: Forecast of water-column conditions. It does not measure toxin in seafood and is not a closure or health decision; CDFW and CDPH decide closures and advisories.
A low probability does not mean an area is safe.
Published skill assessment covers C-HARM v1 (Anderson et al. 2016); no published skill assessment for v3.1 was found.
The producer notes salinity errors can affect domoic acid predictions and that bloom predictions include many false positives.
Issue date is inferred (nowcast valid day + 1). C-HARM does not publish an issue time.

layers.title: Satellite chlorophyll-a (VIIRS, NOAA-20)
layers.description: Daily ocean-colour chlorophyll-a from VIIRS on NOAA-20, rendered by NASA GIBS. A measure of algae biomass near the surface.

freshness.note: Daily satellite composites usually appear 1-3 days after observation. Current: observed within 4 days. Stale: 5-10 days. Historical: older.

tiles.date_selection: Newest date advertised by GetCapabilities was 2026-10-07. Chosen date is the most recent of up to 7 days whose 3 probe tiles over central California returned HTTP 200 palette PNGs with data in at least 2% of pixels.

caveats: Chlorophyll measures algae biomass. It does not measure toxins and does not predict where fish are.
Clouds and fog leave gaps; a gap means no observation, not low chlorophyll.
Browse imagery for visual context. Colours follow NASA's legend; values are not read from these tiles.
